prompt: What does a dbt test's compiled SQL return when the test passes?
hint: It selects the rows that break the rule.

choices.text: One row saying true
choices.why: It returns the failing rows, so none.

choices.text: The model's rows
choices.why: Only the ones that break the rule.

choices.text: No rows
choices.why: Right. Zero rows is a pass.

choices.text: A count of the rows checked
choices.why: dbt counts the failing rows itself.

prompt: How many orders had no customer in the first `dbt test`?
Why did `not_null` on `customer_id` fail for thousands of orders?
hint: Look at which shops they came from.

choices.text: The bookshops' tills sell to people who give no name
choices.why: Right. The rule was wrong, not the data.

choices.text: The loader lost the customers on the way from the shop to raw
choices.why: raw has what the shop has.

choices.text: The website's customers were deleted by a bug in the shop
choices.why: The website had seven, and those were erasures.

choices.text: dbt's view drops nulls
choices.why: Views return what the table has.

prompt: `unique` on `stg_order_lines.order_id` failed. What was wrong?
hint: What is the grain of the model?

choices.text: There are duplicate lines in the shop
choices.why: The pair order and line passed.

choices.text: The relationships test interfered with it
choices.why: Tests are independent queries.

choices.text: The view was out of date
choices.why: Views are read live.

choices.text: The test checked the wrong key
choices.why: Right. One row per order line: the key is the order and the line.

prompt: A test is right and the data breaks it. What should happen to the test?
hint: Where do the bad rows come from?

choices.text: Narrow it until it passes
choices.why: That hides a true failure.

choices.text: It stays as it is; the fix goes upstream
choices.why: Right. Silencing a true test is never right.

choices.text: Delete it until the data is fixed, then write it again from scratch
choices.why: Then nothing would say when they are.

choices.text: Make it a warning permanently
choices.why: A warning is for known, explained exceptions.

prompt: What does `where: "shop_id = 7"` do to a `not_null` test?

choices.text: Deletes the other shops' orders
choices.why: Tests never change data.

choices.text: Checks only the website's orders
choices.why: Right. The model is filtered before the check.

choices.text: Makes the test a warning
choices.why: That is severity.

choices.text: Runs the test only on Sundays, when the website alone is open for business
choices.why: It filters rows, not days.

prompt: How many web orders without a customer did the narrowed test find?
Why not add the seven erased orders to the test's `where`, so that it passes?
hint: What would the next one look like?

choices.text: The where clause cannot list ids
choices.why: It can; the problem is what it hides.

choices.text: dbt forbids where on not_null
choices.why: Ana used one.

choices.text: Erased customers must make every build fail
choices.why: They are lawful; a warning is enough.

choices.text: It would hide the next order that loses its customer for a reason nobody intended
choices.why: Right. Known exceptions belong in a warning, still counted.

prompt: A test on `stg_orders` fails with severity error during `dbt build`. What happens to `daily_sales`?

choices.text: It is skipped and keeps its old rows
choices.why: Right. Nothing downstream of a failed test is built.

choices.text: It is built anyway, from the views as they stand at that moment
choices.why: Its upstream failed a test, so it is skipped.

choices.text: It is emptied
choices.why: Skipping touches nothing.

choices.text: It is dropped, and rebuilt by the next successful run of dbt
choices.why: A skipped model is left as it was.

prompt: What does `severity: warn` change?

choices.text: The test is no longer run
choices.why: It runs and reports every time.

choices.text: The failing rows are deleted
choices.why: Tests never change data.

choices.text: A failure is reported and nothing is skipped
choices.why: Right. The count still shows in every build.

choices.text: It fails only on the first build of the day
choices.why: Severity has no clock.

prompt: What is a singular test?

choices.text: A generic test used once
choices.why: It is written as its own query.

choices.text: A Python function
choices.why: It is SQL.

choices.text: A test that runs on its own, outside dbt build, whenever its file is changed
choices.why: dbt build runs it after the models it refers to.

choices.text: A select returning the wrong rows, with any joins it needs
choices.why: Right. Like drift.sql, with refs.

prompt: After four more days of trade, how many days did the drift test find wrong?
Why does the drift test name `fact_sales` through `ref` rather than as `dbt_marts.fact_sales`?

choices.text: A test cannot read a schema directly
choices.why: It could; it would just not be ordered.

choices.text: So dbt runs it after fact_sales is built
choices.why: Right. The ref puts it in the graph after the model.

choices.text: It makes the test a warning
choices.why: Severity is separate.

choices.text: ref is faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.
